newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares set new record, consolidation ahead.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares set new record, consolidation ahead.

text.p: The Belgian blue-chip index which set a record all-time high on Wednesday was seen remaining cautious in coming days, as investors await more data from the U.S., dealers said.

The Bel-20 .BFX which closed up 0.60 percent at 2,171.11, with a strong 2.96 billion francs volume of Belgian shares traded, was aided by a bullish dollar and particularly by Belgian financials in late trade.
"We're now in a day-to-day market where people are looking at quality stocks, looking at the results, and keeping an eye on the possibility of a correction in the U.S.," said one trader.
"We'll consolidate at these levels with possibilities of further limited rises if Wall Street looks good, the Fed has good news and interest rates remain low," said one trader.
Wall Street took heart from U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's reasurring comments on the stock market earlier today to rise in early trade.
But investors were still nervously awaiting Greenspan's deliverance of the second part of his testimony on the economy at 1900 GMT and U.S. non-payroll data due out on Friday.
Shares in bank BBL closed up 3.41 percent at 8,190 francs after it announced net profit rose 15.1 percent for 1996.
Dealers said BBL's 1996 group net profit of 10.29 billion Belgian francs were according to market expectations and welcomed.
Holding company Groupe Bruxelles Lambert SA (GBL) jumped 5.1 percent to 5,150 francs on speculations it was about to sell its stake in BBL.
Elsewhere glassmaker Glaverbel climbed 4.0 percent to 4,515 francs on renewed interest in cyclical stocks.
